topic: Characteristics of the Indian Economy & Development

items.front: Economic growth vs economic development — the key difference?
items.back: Growth = quantitative rise in real per-capita income. Development = growth + lower poverty/inequality/unemployment + welfare (broader).
items.source: APPSC GK — Growth & Development

items.front: Current GVA shares of the three sectors in India (approx)?
items.back: Services ~54.7%, Industry ~27.6%, Agriculture ~17.7%.
items.examPoint: Sectoral GVA share vs workforce share (current data)
items.source: MoSPI / Economic Survey

items.front: Why is India's agriculture sector marked by low productivity?
items.back: Workforce share ~44–46% but GVA share only ~18% — the wide gap signals low output-per-worker and disguised unemployment.
items.source: MoSPI / Economic Survey

items.front: State the four national-income identities linking GDP, GNP, NNP, NDP.
items.back: GNP = GDP + NFIA; NDP = GDP − Depreciation; NNP = GNP − Depreciation; NNP at factor cost = National Income.
items.examPoint: National income aggregates — GDP, GNP, NNP, NDP
items.source: APPSC GK — Macroeconomics I

items.front: Market price → factor cost conversion?
items.back: Factor cost = Market price − Indirect taxes + Subsidies.
items.examPoint: GNP = GDP + NFIA; market price vs factor cost
items.source: APPSC GK — Macroeconomics I

items.front: GDP deflator formula and India's base year?
items.back: Deflator = (Nominal GDP ÷ Real GDP) × 100; base year 2022-23 (new series from Feb 2026, replacing 2011-12).
items.examPoint: Nominal vs real GDP & GDP deflator
items.source: APPSC GK — Macroeconomics I

items.front: The three methods of estimating national income?
items.back: Production/value-added (ΣGVA); Income (wages+rent+interest+profit); Expenditure (C+I+G+(X−M)).
items.examPoint: GVA & three methods of national income estimation
items.source: APPSC GK — Macroeconomics I & II

items.front: Name the Eight Core Industries.
items.back: Electricity, Steel, Refinery products, Crude oil, Coal, Cement, Natural gas, Fertilizers.
items.examPoint: Core industries — Index of Eight Core Industries
items.source: APPSC GK — Sectors of Indian Economy

items.front: HDI — dimensions, publisher, and India's HDR 2025 standing?
items.back: Health + Education + Standard of living (GNI pc); UNDP; India 0.685, rank 130/193 (Medium).
items.examPoint: HDI — UNDP, three dimensions & India's rank
items.source: UNDP HDR 2025

items.front: Quaternary vs quinary sector?
items.back: Quaternary = knowledge/information services (R&D, IT). Quinary = top-level decision-making/policy ('gold-collar').
items.source: APPSC GK — Sectors of Indian Economy

items.front: Demographic dividend — meaning and precondition?
items.back: Growth boost from a rising working-age (15–59) share vs dependents; realised only with skilling, health and jobs.
items.source: APPSC GK — Growth & Development

items.front: SIT on Black Money (2014) — who headed it and why formed?
items.back: Justice M. B. Shah; formed May 2014 on a Supreme Court direction to trace undisclosed domestic/foreign wealth.
items.examPoint: Black money — meaning, causes & SIT on Black Money (2014, Justice M.B. Shah)
items.source: Ministry of Finance / SC of India

items.front: PMLA 2002 — enforcing agency and the three laundering stages?
items.back: Enforcement Directorate (ED); Placement → Layering → Integration; FIU-IND gets suspicious-transaction reports.
items.source: PMLA 2002 / ED

items.front: Which 2015 law targets undisclosed foreign income and assets?
items.back: Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015.
items.examPoint: Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) Act, 2015
items.source: Ministry of Finance

items.front: AP economy: GSDP, per-capita income, and how its GSVA differs from all-India?
items.back: GSDP ~₹19.75 lakh cr (2026-27); per-capita ~₹2.98 lakh (above national); primary sector ~35–37% of GSVA (vs ~18% all-India).
items.examPoint: Andhra Pradesh GSDP & per-capita income (latest) — ~₹19.75 lakh cr, ~₹2.98 lakh per capita
items.source: PRS AP Budget 2026-27; AP Socio-Economic Survey

items.front: Traditional approach to economic development — what does it say?
items.back: Development = a sustained increase in real per capita income; growth and development are used as synonyms.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Which output-related change does development include but growth does not?
items.back: Change in the composition of output and allocation of resources across sectors (agriculture, industry, etc.).
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Why is development harder to achieve than growth?
items.back: It needs changes in social structure, attitudes and institutions, not just more output from more inputs.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Define ICOR. Is a high ICOR good or bad?
items.back: ICOR = extra investment ÷ extra output. High ICOR = more capital per unit of output = inefficient (bad).
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Which four development indices does the source list?
items.back: HDI, IHDI (inequality-adjusted), GDI (gender development) and AHDI (Augmented HDI).
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Who gave the three-sector (primary-secondary-tertiary) classification?
items.back: A.G.B. Fisher and Colin Clark — the Fisher-Clark hypothesis of sectoral shift.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Who gave the dual-sector (surplus labour) model of development?
items.back: W. Arthur Lewis (1954): surplus labour shifts from the traditional subsistence sector to the modern sector.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Rostow's stages of economic growth?
items.back: Traditional society → pre-conditions → take-off → drive to maturity → high mass consumption.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Amartya Sen's view of development?
items.back: Capability approach — 'Development as Freedom': expanding the real freedoms people enjoy.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: GNP counts production by whom?
items.back: By the nationals of a country — whether they live within the country or outside it (GNP = GDP + NFIA).
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Why are only final goods counted in GDP?
items.back: To avoid double counting of intermediate goods (raw materials already included in the value of final goods).
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Sugar mill turning sugarcane into sugar — which sector?
items.back: Secondary sector — a raw material (sugarcane) is processed into sugar or gur.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Defining feature of the tertiary sector?
items.back: Also called the service sector — supports primary and secondary production and produces no tangible goods.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Give four modern IT-based tertiary activities named in the source.
items.back: Internet cafes, ATM booths, call centres and software companies.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Why has the tertiary sector grown fastest in India?
items.back: IT boom, higher urbanisation and increased consumer spending on services.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Three examples of unorganised-sector workers?
items.back: Daily wage labourers, street vendors and owners of small unregistered shops.

items.front: Share of India's workers in informal employment (latest ILO)?
items.back: About 87% (ILO 2025) — roughly 80–90% of all workers are informal.

items.front: Public vs private sector — two examples each from the source?

items.front: What is a sunrise industry?
items.back: A sector in its infancy with high growth potential — e.g. IT, healthcare, telecom, infrastructure, retail.

items.front: White-collar vs blue-collar?
items.back: White-collar = professional/office (accountants, lawyers). Blue-collar = manual and skilled trades (electricians, plumbers).
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Economics: Growth and Development.txt, Sectors of Indian Economy.txt; NCERT Indian Economic Development (Class XI) / Ramesh Singh standard treatment; IMF WEO Apr 2026; UNDP HDR 2025; PRS AP Budget 2026-27; PYQ bank .research/pyq-bank/econ-characteristics-development.md

items.front: Red-collar and black-collar jobs?
items.back: Red-collar = government and emergency services (police). Black-collar = hazardous/informal work (miners, sanitation workers).

items.front: What is black money?
items.back: Income or wealth on which due tax has not been paid or which is concealed from the authorities — the parallel economy.
